answer: Agents can require a fresh, publicly verifiable proof of personhood before an account may claim a scarce, transferable reputation credential. One person can obtain only one credential per epoch; issuing it costs a small fee and requires an in-person check, while credential transfers are barred. A comet-themed cipher or glacier-themed account name changes nothing: each extra identity must pass another check, so the attacker pays repeated fees and bears the real-world cost of recruiting distinct people.
